$comment: State encoding, transcribed from spec/REPRESENTATION.md and spec/STATE_MODEL.md. Prose wins on disagreement.

_meta.authority: This file is a faithful transcription for mechanization consumers. Where it disagrees with spec/, the prose wins and this file must be fixed.
_meta.representation: sparse supports over qubit indices; the encoding qldpc-challenge already ships an archived note for its own codes, which this file does not transcribe.

Q.description: Qubit namespace. A finite set of naturals, encoded as a strictly increasing list. Explicitly NOT the range 0..n-1, so C-DIRECT-SUM is a plain disjoint union with no relabelling step.

rows.description: The display. UNORDERED: state identity does not depend on row order or matrix layout (FD1 exit condition).

id.description: Stable generator identifier. Injective on live rows; never reused (I3).

sector.description: Sector label, matching the row space the row spans (I4). Explicit rather than inferred from position, so a malformed state is representable and can be rejected.

support.description: One stabilizer as the list of qubits it acts on. Strictly increasing, no repeats. Subsets of Q.

used.description: Every identifier ever minted on this state: live union retired. SEMANTIC, not provenance . Read by the canonical mint, by state equality, and by the C-DIRECT-SUM disjointness premise.

state.formalization_status: Partial mechanization present under lean/ (state model, canonical mint, term language, invariants, and a soundness slice); see lean/README.md. Not a proof of soundness.

derived_not_stored.k: k = n - dim(rows_X) - dim(rows_Z), where dim is GF(2) rank of the display. I1 makes the display spanning, so rank of the display IS rank of the row space.
derived_not_stored.w: w = max { wt(r) : r in rows } (0 if the display is empty). Max stabilizer weight; derived, exact, not a state field, not minted or transported by used .
derived_not_stored.r: r = max { diam_lambda(s) : s in rows } (0 if the display is empty), where diam_lambda is the largest Euclidean distance between two points of a row's support in a supplied layout lambda. Derived, exact, not a state field, not minted or transported by used . A function of the PAIR (state, layout), so a state with no layout has no radius; the layout is ledger data, not state data.
derived_not_stored.note: qldpc-challenge declares n and k as fields. Here they are redundant declared values that must agree with the computed ones. Disagreement is a MALFORMED input, not a value adopted.

I1_WellFormedCSS.statement: X = <rows_X> and Z = <rows_Z>, and X is orthogonal to Z. Nontrivial X intersect Z is permitted.
I1_WellFormedCSS.note: The span clause is DEFINITIONAL . The row space IS the span of the display; this is not a property of the display.

invariants.I2_displayed_independence: Each displayed row is not in the span of the other displayed rows of its sector.
invariants.I3_identifier_discipline: id is injective on live rows; a retired identifier is never reused; fresh identifiers are minted canonically as the first element of a fixed enumeration not in `used`. There is no fresh-name choice anywhere, so every primitive is deterministic outright.
invariants.I4_sector_typing: Every displayed row carries exactly one sector label, matching the row space it spans.
invariants.I5_valid_provenance: Provenance records are append-only and refer only to identifiers live or retired at the recorded step. Steps are read by nothing else: no Eval premise and no judgment reads them.

equality.definition: C1 equiv C2 iff identical Q AND identical labeled rows AND identical used.
consequences: Q is part of identity: states with the same labeled rows and used set on different namespaces differ in n, k, and applicability, and are not equal .
used is part of identity: a state reached by a delete/add loop is NOT equal to its origin even when the row space is restored.
row order is not part of identity, and Q is read as a set.

not_represented.phases: Phase-insensitive (FD1). Y-type behaviour arises from X intersect Z, never from an explicit phase.
not_represented.distance: d_X, d_Z, d are not state fields. The separate consumer ledger carries sourced intervals and witnesses; transitions do not search exact distance. External lower bounds, exact prices, and minimum-weight-class enumerations are explicit judgment inputs and are not verified by the consumer.
not_represented.Pi_fields: Interfaces, boundaries, metrics, logical witnesses, certificates, constructor inputs, inversion data. None are MVP data.
not_represented.layout: The geometric placement of the qubits is not carried by this encoding. It is LEDGER DATA, not a Pi field: supplied per code and held beside the state, so two states differing only in their layout are the same state.

evaluator_contract.spanning: ASSUMED, not checked. The evaluator trusts the span clause of I1 (definitional, so not checkable) and verifies I1's orthogonality clause plus I2-I5.
evaluator_contract.cost_of_that_decision: Sound on spanning displays only. Given a non-spanning independent display it computes a k that does not correspond to a code and reports transformations whose premises were decided against the wrong row space. That is a silent wrong answer, not an error.
evaluator_contract.available_but_unused: Rank arithmetic over the incidence matrix is the same computation the derivation uses, and would turn the assumption into a precondition. Not done in the MVP because I1 makes it redundant.
evaluator_contract.formalization_status: WP0-WP1 present under lean/ (state model, canonical mint, term language, I1-I5, Eval skeleton), plus the first derivation-layer soundness slice (lean/CodeCalculus/Soundness.lean, 2026-10-25), stated for a well-formed evaluation chain with the evaluation assumed; not a proof of soundness.
evaluator_contract.consumer_status: Executable interval consumer present at machine/priced_calculus.py; this is not a proof assistant and does not establish soundness.

fields: the supplied layout, as ledger data
the interaction radius recomputed against it
consumer_ledger.trust_boundary: The consumer validates witnesses and structural consistency but does not validate supplied lower bounds, exact prices, or exhaustive enumerations.

E-GRAFT.rows: Retire every selected-sector row touching q; add canonically minted adjacent products restricted to Q\{q}; retain other selected-sector rows; shorten opposite-sector rows at q.
E-GRAFT.ids: Retired IDs remain in used; add IDs minted in canonical order.

P-REBASE.rows: retire the selected sector's displayed rows; mint canonically named GL(m,2) combinations of them (identifiers minted canonically); opposite sector rows untouched
P-REBASE.ids: retired IDs remain in used; minted IDs added
P-REBASE.used: retain retired identifiers and add minted identifiers

E-LOCAL-HADAMARD.rows: swap the sector label of every displayed row; supports, identifiers and used unchanged

E-PEEL.rows: retire the unique selected-sector row touching q; shorten opposite-sector rows at q; other selected-sector rows unchanged
E-PEEL.ids: retired ID remains in used; no mint

E-PUNCTURE.rows: delete every displayed row (both sectors) whose support contains q; surviving rows are q-free and retained
E-PUNCTURE.ids: retired IDs remain in used; no mint

E-EXTEND.Q: add the disjoint qubit set Delta
E-EXTEND.rows: append canonically minted (sector, support) rows over Q union Delta; factor rows unchanged
E-EXTEND.ids: mint one identifier per addition in canonical order
E-EXTEND.used: retain old used and add minted identifiers

E-GLUE.Q: union of the two factor namespaces
E-GLUE.rows: factor rows followed by one canonically minted row per admissible seam check; no factor row removed or altered
E-GLUE.ids: mint one identifier per seam check over the union of the factors' used sets
E-GLUE.used: union of the factors' used sets plus minted seam identifiers
